content.title: Lower Mortgage Rates, Higher Prices? How Trump’s Plan Affects First-Time Buyers
content.summary: Trump's plan to block investors from the housing market might actually make homes more expensive to buyers, unless supply can be increased to meet high demand.

content.title: Bond-Market Contrarians Look to Buy US 30-Year Near 5% Yield
content.summary: The strategy, from money managers including Columbia Threadneedle Investment and Wellington Management, runs counter to the consensus wager, which is that lengthier tenors will suffer in 2026, especially compared to shorter counterparts, steepening the yield curve.  The contrarian approach is gaining relevance after a selloff in Treasuries last week drove 30-year yields toward 5%, the highest since September, before purchasers emerged.  For Ed Al-Hussainy, a portfolio manager at Columbia Threadneedle, it makes sense to go against the herd.

content.title: Trump’s housing market plan contains a fatal flaw and multiple obstacles, Morgan Stanley says
content.summary: "Affordability in U.S. housing is a tricky issue that lacks a silver bullet," the bank said. Trump's actions are only "modestly helpful" for affordability.

thumbnail.caption: President Donald Trump has been making moves in the housing market.

content.title: Trump housing finance chief OKs more mortgage spending and adds risk for government-backed lenders
content.summary: President Donald Trump's federal housing finance director, Bill Pulte, quietly granted government-backed lenders the authority to nearly double a $200 billion bond purchase that Trump ordered to try to lower mortgage rates, a move that could introduce a new level of risk for the companies.  An email obtained by The Associated Press that was sent by the Federal Housing Finance Agency to top officials at Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac eliminated caps that prohibited the lenders from each holding more than $40 billion in mortgage bonds.

content.title: How Trump’s US$200 Billion MBS Push And Housing Curbs At FNMA Have Changed Its Investment Story
content.summary: Earlier this week, President Donald Trump ordered Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to purchase up to US$200 billion of mortgage-backed securities, while moving to restrict large institutional investors from buying single-family homes and exploring access to 401(k) savings for down payments. This policy mix could significantly reshape how credit flows into the US housing market, expanding Fannie Mae’s policy role while challenging Wall Street’s presence in single-family rentals. content.title: BitGo Stock Rises After IPO, Defying Recent Crypto Downturn
content.summary: Shares of BitGo traded 25% higher in the crypto-infrastructure firm’s New York Stock Exchange debut, marking the first major test for a digital-asset company IPO since the sector’s market downturn last year.

content.title: Trump pushes for lower rates and ban on investor home purchases in bid to make homes more affordable
content.summary: President Donald Trump 's plans for bringing homeownership within reach of more Americans involve pushing for lower interest rates on home loans and credit cards, and banning large institutional investors from buying single-family homes.  In his address Wednesday at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, Trump outlined four policies his administration is pursuing in a bid to make homeownership more affordable.  The U.S. housing market has been in a sales slump dating back to 2022, when mortgage rates began to climb from pandemic-era lows.

content.title: Trump doesn’t want America to be ‘a nation of renters,’ but experts say at least one of his proposals may put homeownership more out of reach
content.summary: Experts told Fortune Trump’s proposal allowing Americans to tap their 401(k) for down payments could inflate prices and leave Americans poorer in retirement.

content.title: Executive Order Takes a Step Toward Ban on Big Investors Buying Single-Family Homes
content.summary: The White House moved toward implementing President Donald Trump's ban on large institutional investors buying single-family homes in an executive order issued Tuesday night.  The first step is deciding what "large institutional investor" and "single-family home" actually mean.  The order, issued before Trump speaks about affordability at the World Economic Forum, charges the Treasury secretary and the assistant to the president for economic policy with developing definitions of "large institutional investor" and "single family home" within thirty days.

content.title: Lower Mortgage Rates Were Fun While They Lasted. It’s Over for Now.
